SMTO-SKL-0092 — The Microsoft sign-in took too long and expired

GUID: 57408641-976e-582d-a2c8-abc5823e1ece
Slug: microsoft365-oauth-timeout
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Each Microsoft sign-in link works for ten minutes. You came back after that, so SMTO didn't connect the account and saved nothing new.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close the old Microsoft sign-in tab, then ask the Agent again to connect your Microsoft 365 account. An expired link can't be reused; a new request gives you a fresh ten-minute window.
  2. Open the new link right away, sign in, and approve the permissions Microsoft shows. The sign-in only completes if you get back to SMTO before the link expires.

What success looks like

  • The browser page says your account is connected and you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • If Microsoft keeps asking for extra approval from your organization, ask your Microsoft administrator. Otherwise select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The shared BrowserOAuth handshake reached its ten-minute lifetime before a callback arrived (authorization_timeout, mapped to microsoft365.oauth_timeout); no tokens were exchanged or saved.

What this means

  • The shared browser OAuth lifecycle reports authorization_timeout, which Microsoft maps to oauth_timeout. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • The shared browser OAuth lifecycle reports authorization_timeout, which Microsoft maps to oauth_timeout.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original consent request's lifetime and current flow state.

How to fix it

  • Call microsoft365.connect again to create a fresh single-use consent request and complete Microsoft's consent within ten minutes. Expired handshakes are discarded from memory; nothing was written to Parameter Store.
  • Start a fresh connect flow when ready and complete that exact callback within ten minutes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A new single-use consent flow completes within its ten-minute lifetime.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
